What changed since CRAN 0.3.2

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-changes.qmd

CRAN has medfit 0.3.2; this site documents 0.11.1 (GitHub and r-universe). This page lists what a 0.3.2 user needs to know before upgrading: numbers that change, calls that now stop with an error, and what is new. The full record is NEWS.

The short version

  • Two results were wrong in 0.3.2 and are fixed: serial te()/pm(), and confint(parm = "paths") on lavaan-extracted objects. See issue #83.
  • Several silent mistakes now stop with an error. If code that ran before fails now, check the second table.
  • Install from r-universe or GitHub; see the home page.

Numbers that change

Version What Before Now
0.5.0 serial te() and pm() summed only the chain and the direct effect (a * d * b + c'), leaving out paths that skip a mediator sum every path from treatment to outcome; te() equals the treatment coefficient of lm(Y ~ X + covariates) when the models are linear with the same covariates
0.5.0 confint(parm = "paths") looked for lm-style row names only; on lavaan-extracted objects the b and c' standard errors were swapped finds each path by name, and stops with an error naming the missing rows
0.5.0 confint(parm = "effects") for a simple fit the total-effect interval was too wide (it dropped the covariance of the indirect effect and c') full delta-method gradient; on the mediation_demo fit the total-effect SE is 0.119, not 0.127
0.5.0 four-way decomposition with factor or transformed covariates the covariate means skipped them, so NDE, INTref and the total were wrong means come from the mediator model’s design matrix; with weights, they are weighted
0.8.0 nobs(), @n_obs and med() when the data have missing values on a model variable counted nrow(data) although glm() had dropped the incomplete rows: 5 missing treatment values in 400 rows gave 400 count the rows the models used (395 in that example); fit_mediation() drops rows that are incomplete on any variable in either formula before fitting, so both models share one sample
0.9.0 standard errors of INTref, NDE and the total effect from extract_mediation() of a lavaan four-way fit when the mediator equation has a covariate left out the covariate-mean term, so they were too small: INTref SE 0.022 against 0.069 from lavaan’s own := (measured on 0.8.0; 0.3.2 has no tidy() for these objects) equal lavaan’s := (0.069)
0.9.0 INTref from a lavaan four-way fit with sampling weights used unweighted covariate means, so it differed from the lm/glm route: 0.726 against 0.841 on the check data uses the weighted means and equals the lm/glm route (0.841)
0.8.0 the names in coef(), vcov() and tidy() of a SEMFit an unlabeled parameter was "M ~ X" or "X ~~ X" (with spaces) and a loading "m2 ~ eta" "M~X", "X~~X" and "eta=~m2", the names lavaan::coef() uses; labeled parameters are unchanged
0.9.0 a fixed intercept, y ~ 0*1, in the native engine the row was dropped and the covariance-only fit returned a restriction (“the mean of y is 0”): one degree of freedom, a changed discrepancy, comparable with anova(); any y ~ 1 row turns the mean structure on
0.9.0 logLik(), AIC(), BIC() of a native fit with fixed_x (new argument) conditional on the fixed variables; anova(), mbco_sem() and multi-fit AIC()/BIC() stop when fixed sets or data differ; glance() gains a fixed_x column
0.10.0 extract_mediation(<SEMFit>, decomposition = "four_way") refused by name until the : operator existed returns the four-way decomposition when the outcome equation carries the treatment-by-mediator product; refused with a message that says to add x:m when it does not
0.5.0 se_type = "sandwich" with a treatment-by-mediator term returned the model-based covariance, with no warning applies the sandwich estimator
0.5.0 lavaan fits with custom path labels the alias rows of @vcov were all zero, so a parametric bootstrap had a zero-width interval the alias rows are filled from the labeled parameters

What did not change: nie() for serial objects still returns the chain effect by default. The new nie(x, type = "total") returns the total indirect effect.

If you stored serial te() or pm() values from 0.4.0 or earlier, rerun them.

Names that changed

Code that reads a result by column name, or passes an argument by name, breaks silently when the name changes. These two renames are the ones to search your scripts for.

Version What Before Now
0.9.0 tidy() columns std.error, conf.low, conf.high (and p.value for a SEMFit, which exists from 0.7.0) std_error, conf_low, conf_high, p_value; glance() of a SEMFit has p_value too; mbco_sem() keeps p.value because it returns a base-R htest
0.9.0 tidy() arguments conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.9 conf_int = TRUE, conf_level = 0.9; the dotted names still work and warn (is deprecated as of medfit 0.9.0)
0.9.0 class of a summary() result summary.MediationData summary_MediationData (likewise summary_SEMFit and the other classes)
0.8.0 fit_sem(sampling_weights = ), only for code written against 0.7.0 the argument name in 0.7.0 fit_sem(weights = ), the name fit_mediation() uses; the old name still works and warns once per session

Calls that now stop with an error

Each of these was accepted before and gave a wrong or ignored result.

Version Call Message to look for What to do
0.5.0 m_star supplied with no treatment-by-mediator term applies only when the outcome model has a treatment-by-mediator drop m_star, or add the product term
0.5.0 a product written inside a function, such as I(X * M) Found function-wrapped treatment-by-mediator product term(s) write it as X * M or X:M
0.5.0 a product among mediators in a multi-mediator model Multi-mediator (serial or parallel) extraction supports only treatment-by-mediator product terms refit without it; a treatment-by-mediator product in the outcome model is supported (see Joint mediation)
0.5.0 four-way decomposition with a non-identity link Four-way decomposition requires the identity link refit with gaussian(link = "identity")
0.7.0 a glm() argument passed through ... that partly matches model, such as mod = FALSE is only used with engine = "native" drop the argument; glm()’s own model cannot be passed through fit_mediation()
0.9.0 a lavaan four-way fit that has a product of the treatment with a covariate in the mediator or the outcome equation (m ~ x + xc) does not support a treatment product it changed the effects without changing a coefficient the decomposition reads, and 0.8.0 returned a decomposition without a message; remove the product, or fit without the four-way decomposition
0.11.0 AIC() or BIC() of several SEMFits over different observed variables, such as a fit with a product term and one without different observed variables the likelihoods describe different data, so they are not comparable; compare fits over the same variables (anova() and mbco_sem() refuse the same pair)
0.11.1 anova() of two SEMFits where a nonzero fixed parameter (for example M1 ~~ 0.5*M2) is in one fit and absent from the other nonzero fixed parameters differ fit the restricted model by fixing or constraining parameters of the larger one, so both fits carry the same fixed values

Two more stop in situations 0.3.2 could not reach: two lmer fits that kept different individuals within the same clusters (0.6.0), and a lavaan label that reuses one of medfit’s alias names for a different path (0.5.0).

Objects that gained something

Version What Effect on your code
0.5.0 serial objects gain a nie_total row in tidy(), a nie_total column in glance(), and indirect_total in coef(type = "effects") appended after the existing entries, so positions are unchanged
0.7.0 a lavaan fit of a simple single-mediator model appends the rows m_<treatment>, y_<mediator> and y_<treatment> to @estimates and @vcov code that indexes these by position past the a, b, c_prime rows sees three more rows; code that looks rows up by name is fine

What is new

Version New
0.4.0 the regmedint engine, engine_args, and m_star in fit_mediation(); see The regmedint engine
0.5.0 joint mediation (page); the bundled mediation_demo data; delta-method standard errors in tidy(); confint() and coef() for bootstrap results
0.6.0 cluster-randomized designs (page); the Reference Card and Cookbook
0.7.0 the native maximum-likelihood engine (page), mbco_sem(), and sampling weights with robust standard errors for it
0.8.0 nonlinear constraints in the native engine (page), mbco_sem(paths = ) for a product of k paths, anova(), tidy()/glance()/confint() for SEMFit, lavaan and the native engine, and cookbook recipes 12 and 13
0.9.0 observed intercepts and means in the native engine (y ~ 1, meanstructure =), fixed_x (page), cookbook recipe 18 and step 9 of the native tutorial
0.10.0 the product term x:m in native syntax and the four-way decomposition from a native fit (extract_mediation() on a fit_sem() fit), a supported-class table, and a worked example in the interaction page
0.11.0 categorical covariates in native syntax (page, recipe 21); options(medfit.covariate_mean_variance = TRUE) for population-average four-way standard errors (default unchanged); AIC()/BIC() refuse fits over different observed variables; nonlinear-constrained fits no longer wander to negative variances (#213); the native engine is no longer marked experimental (its signatures, SEMFit properties and syntax change only through a deprecation)

Dependencies

0.7.0 adds lifecycle and nloptr (>= 1.0.4) to Imports, and OpenMx to Suggests (the tests use it as an independent check). 0.8.0 adds withr to Suggests (tests only).
